title: Length bound from a power witness
statement: Let $z$ and $S$ be finite bit strings, and suppose there are bit strings $E$, $b$, and $a$ such that $S$ is the pairing of the total second projection of the total second projection of $z$ with the nested pair consisting of $E$ and the pair $(b,a)$. Require that the length of $E$ is at most the length of the total first projection of the total second projection of $z$, that $b$ and $a$ are the canonical bit strings obtained by writing their respective values in binary, that the length of $b$ is at most the sum of the lengths of the total first projection of $z$ and the total second projection of the total second projection of $z$, and that the length of $a$ is at most one plus the length of the total second projection of the total second projection of $z$. If the value of that latter projection is positive, require also that the values of $b$ and $a$ are both smaller than it and that the value of $a$ times the value of $b$ raised to the value of $E$ is congruent modulo it to the value of the total first projection of $z$ raised to the value of the total first projection of the total second projection of $z$. Then the length of $S$ is at most $9$ times the sum of the length of $z$ and one.
hypotheses_covered: There exist bit strings $E,b,a$ with the specified nested pairing encoding of $S$
If $\operatorname{val}(\pi_2(\pi_2(z)))>0$, then $\operatorname{val}(b)$ and $\operatorname{val}(a)$ are each smaller than $\operatorname{val}(\pi_2(\pi_2(z)))$

Under the same positivity condition, $\operatorname{val}(a)\operatorname{val}(b)^{\operatorname{val}(E)}$ is congruent to $\operatorname{val}(\pi_1(z))^{\operatorname{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(z)))}$ modulo $\operatorname{val}(\pi_2(\pi_2(z)))$
